ideas.title: The suitcase island
ideas.critique: The island shown inside itself is the TV post's trick, and drawing the scene twice at 1/40 scale is plain instancing that a viewer can mistake for a toy model. What is strong is the coupling running both ways: the giant face leaning in from the sky and a poke at the tiny sea rippling the big one. Those two moments are the whole idea, and without them it is a diorama in a box.

ideas.title: Melting noon
ideas.critique: The plainest version is a vertex shear scaled by the time of day, and that reads as a wobbly shader, not things going soft. What the island never had is bodies sagging under their own weight and then keeping new shapes that pile up day after day, so the island visibly drifts. That only works if the slump has real weight and the permanent changes can be read the next day.

ideas.title: The hat tower
ideas.critique: This is round 1's Hat thief with a verlet spine and thrown berries added, so it is the same cartoon gag of a crab hoarding loot. It still depends entirely on the sway and the slow felled-tree topple looking heavy. The berry hit that brings it down is the only new interaction, and hats landing on the wrong heads is a joke you can predict.

ideas.title: Keeper of the beam
ideas.critique: This is round 1's lighthouse statues with the player holding the beam, and the rules are still a children's game that most people know. The steps that count are that it can be played, a real stone material taking over a body mid-stride, and creatures that learn to hide behind trees. That hiding has to come from real line-of-sight to the beam, or the friends are just walking a script in the dark.

ideas.title: The pond is two seconds late
ideas.critique: Round 1's lagging pond again, and its core is still the TV's trick of showing the island its own past. The late Gloop climbing out of the water as a second, dripping body that replays the first one's last two seconds is a real twist and the one shot worth making. The testing and waiting will be scripted unless it comes out of what the friends really did.

ideas.title: A shout that shoves
ideas.critique: Speech turned into something physical is the recipe behind the sand dunes and Gloop's "Higher!", with a push in place of a pile. The new part is a refracting ring of air that bends the island behind it in the trace, plus sound that drives the physics. Whether anyone watches it twice depends on how the meadow and the bodies give way under the ring, not on the shouting.
